title: Straightedge-and-Compass Constructibility of the Reciprocal-$k$-th-Power Law
summary: Given positive lengths $a$ and $b$ and a positive integer $k$, let $c$ be determined by $$ \frac{1}{c^k}=\frac{1}{a^k}+\frac{1}{b^k}. $$ We prove that a single finite unmarked-straightedge-and-compass construction producing $c$ for every pair $a,b$ exists if and only if $k$ is a power of two. Necessity follows by specializing to $a=b=1$ and applying the algebraic-degree obstruction to $2^{1/k}$; sufficiency is established by a recursive construction using third, fourth, and mean proportionals.
